biography.plain_text: Rocco Jack Mazreku was an Albanian-born businessman who led the group that took over Porto di Lavagna after its predecessor's collapse. He personally oversaw operations at the large marina on Italy's Ligurian coast until his death in 2013. Responsibility for the company's day-to-day management then passed to his son Matthew.

long_biography.plain_text:
Marina operator Rocco Jack Mazreku concentrated on the practical details that kept Lavagna working. Deteriorating pontoons, unreliable utilities and damaged working areas needed attention. Under his management, repairs strengthened the breakwater, replaced the fuel installation and restored the electrical, water and fire-safety systems.

He also saw a marina as part of a wider local economy, supporting tradespeople and businesses beyond its boundaries. During the boating downturn, he organised Lavagna's first international boat show around used as well as new craft. The format gave brokers and customers time for unhurried conversations, while helping yards find buyers for unsold boats.
